userFeedback: Users who are not using App for Flight booking.
quickObservations:
Found some set of users who are using mobile app for booking flights. Some just rely completely on OTA. 
1. Interestingly, I met a family with 2 kids. Their kids were just engaged with drawing on paper and creating craft on the airport. Parent were chatting. After meeting them they mentioned the reason why they rely on OTA. They never wanted their kids to get distracted because of their phone usage. The family is ready to spend some extra cash but do not want to use phone in front of their kids and wanted to give them full attention when they having a family time. I respect their decision and honestly surprised to met such conscious parents in today's date.
2.
offTheRecord:
Category - Rare - Conscious Family traveller
Name - NA
Location - DEL IGI T1
Trav Context - NA

quickObservations:
1. Have noticed the Marketplace on priority. 
2. Was discussing more about the marketplace only, which depicts (a.) how much we are emphasising on the 6EPick marketplace than main Flight booking; (b.) how users decides their travel plan package. 
3. Realised when users are travelling with family -- (a.) They look forward to leisure and safety along with full package view. (b.) their preferences while booking are Time & money both, so they get enough time when they land and they can travel in day time from family's safety concerns. 
4. Clear suggestion from the user to have personalisation segmentation based on Trip type -- Business/Leisure, so it'll be easy to them for quicker decisions. 
5. User found label 'Experience' a bit of ambiguous 
6. User found 'Offers', 'Loyalty' programs deviation. Despite the user has ~20 flight trips in a year. Majority of them are business trips. For business trips his preferences is Time and not money. 
7. User mentioned he's least interested in IndiGo loyalty program 
8. Observation based on #6 & 7 -- found this consistent behaviour in last couple of interviews also where users are 48+ YO age group); maybe we should leverage this insight for age group wise preferences. 
9. This user prefers to have offers in immediate upfront cash discount. No hidden OR CC based discounts. 
10. As family they mentioned usually when they travel, they do their research beforehand. 
11. User was discussing lot of his experiences during his Homepage visit, that's the reason we can see max time usage of on Homepage. 
12. Requested a feature for long weekend planning. 
13. User is able to understand the entry point for booking. 
14. During family booking the user's preference is Time for family safety & comfort. 
15. User is able to compare the Fare offering differences. 
16. For business trip user prefers upfront seats.

quickObservations:

postTaskAnswers: User is bar-tender by profession. Travelling to Goa from UK. Travels twice a year to India. Price conscious traveller.
quickObservations:
1. User is able to relate Search widget as entry point for booking. 
2. He's a sky scanner user, usually book flight by his own. 
3. Observed the user is taking decision based on the prices mentioned in the calendar. It's noticeable. 
4. In Paymode page, users are able to understand that sector, passenger, calendar cards are tappable. 
5. [User was hesitated to continue his journey, thought he has to pay also. After giving him a confidence, that its a fictious journey he moved further]
6. On SRP page, user expects the full card is tappable. And he can see details. However he's not able to understand the prices & colour bands are tappable. It's a serious usability concern we need to address from user friendly POV. The dropdown chevron's affordance is not prominent enough. 
7. Probable transition on SRP page for Flight card -- Just show expanding it and expanding the categories beneath with details.
offTheRecord:
Category - Individual traveller
Name - BT
Location - DEL IGI T1
Trav Context - UK to Goa with layover in Delhi

postTaskAnswers: User is marine captain, based out of Navi Mumbai.
quickObservations:
1. Personalised welcome message observed by the user
2. Text in the search widget was noticed by the user and understood it’s a start point of Flight booking. 
3. But he called out the hierarchy of 'Recent Search' is too catchy than 'Search widget'
4. User called out -- Font size can be an issue, so slight bigger is better. 
5. User is 50+ and highlighted that 'Offers' are that important for them. 
6. User expects an entry point for contextual help from Trip history. 
7. User was later 'intuitively' be able to find Contact us from Profile menu link, but he did not use search for, instead he scroll all the way down. We need to synthesize -- do we really need so prominent search field on Profile/menu reveal page? 
8. Round trip selection has usability bug -- if user selects start date before selecting the round trip, he expects the next date he selects should be return date. Our system only starts start date after selecting the round trip radio button, hence user goof up while selecting the return date. 
9. On Pay-mode page, user took some time to reconfirm things about the details he filled. The labels (when, who, etc) are making sense to him. 
10. Subtle observation - when user selects 'Economy' in the filter, we still do not reduce the information overload from the SRP and show them Stretch prices and details. It makes sense to underplay non-required info when the contextual filters applied. In this case, Stretch data can be underplayed. This how we reduce unwanted listing, if someone selects 'Morning flight' on SRP, we just show morning flights (and other flights are removed)
11. User struggled to 'Reset filter' after applying multiple filters. Similarly when there was no results after filtering. 
12. User has a fair expectation -- IndiGo is LLC and more people fly in economy, why do you keep 'Stretch (Economy)' as first selector. It should be 'Economy' first. 
13. User is able to observe the difference in Fare family, along with slide/tap gesture.
offTheRecord:
Category - Family travel coordinator
Name - MC
Location - DEL IGI T1
Trav Context - DEL to NMI (returning home)

postTaskAnswers: User is in sales. GoIbibo user. Extreme frequent air traveller. Travel at least twice a week for business. But he books flight by himself only for his person travel. Personal travelling frequency (and booking himself) couple of times in a year.
quickObservations:
1. User noticed 'Recent search' prominently; which means Search widget entry point is underplayed. 
2. User struggled with entry point. 
3. User is persuaded by 6EPick -- Hotel, cabs, etc. 
4. User is relating an entry point for Flight from bottom navbar link. 
5. Despite of label 'Book your flight' user is not able to read it and notice it. We need to address this design issue. 
6. USER IS SUPPORTED WITH HINT FOR START POINT FOR BOOKING [06:36].
7. User confirms, while on business trips, he's conscious about time not prices. 
8. User's quote "why are you asking adult, child etc, when ticket rates are same for all". Subtle insight -- if we are able to establish the relation among 'Selected Names -> Adult/Child/Sr.Citizen data -> Related offers' or a nudges, it'll be better for user. 
9. User's expectation -- shorter journey than it's designed. Design Suggestion -- Can we design 2 & 3 click booking journeys (till SRP) for logged in user? 
10. User is not able to relate with a label 'Cash' on pay mode page. Subtle suggestion -- We have enough space on this screen. Can we establish Cash means every other payment includes CC, QR, UPI etc.? And BluChip redemption can help you saving money. 
11. User is able to figure out filtering. 
12. User quoted "I'm stuck" on SRP page, after trying to tap on card and it's not responding. Price and colour section is not having enough affordance. How can we address that? -- Possible solution nudging user with coach mark if the action is not taken after certain period of time (at least for first couple of times). USER IS SUPPORTED WITH HINT [11:57]

postTaskAnswers: Existing IndiGo mobile power user, frequent traveller. Surprised at first time by seeing the design. Works in Nashik for engineering mfg. company and visiting Delhi for business and visits hometown in Kerala.
quickObservations:
1. Surprised seeing new IndiGo app design. (considering he's existing user)
2. User is able to catch 'Booking entry' in first 15 sec only, because of the Field placeholder label and icon. 
3. Happy to see IBC prominence on homepage. 
4. User was able to find Help, contact us in Profile menu link in 13 sec. But here also he did not use search, instead scroll down till end. Looks like IA is working as everything upfront, but need to synthesise if need to keep search so prominent on profile link page.
5. Subtle suggestion - for calendar page, can we have swipe gesture to change month? and ensure month switching chevron has enough tappable area. 
6. IndiGo Power user expects multi-city trip. 
7. Round trip selection has usability bug -- if user selects start date before selecting the round trip, he expects the next date he selects should be return date. Our system only starts start date after selecting the round trip radio button, hence user goof up while selecting the return date. 
8. User is able to understand that his child will not fit into Children category as the mentioned age group as sub title is making sense. 
9. IndiGo Power user understands what 'Cash' means. And how they can use Cash+BluChip combined. 
10. On SRP, the power user can understand the tappable sections - Economy/Stretch. 
11. It was relatively very easy journey for the IndiGo power user as compare to the user who's new to IndiGo's vocabulary and user interfaces.
offTheRecord:
Category - Power IndiGo user - business traveller
Name - Suresh
Location - DEL IGI T1
Trav Context - DEL to ISK (Going back home after 3 days of office meeting)
